done_when: Find why the test hits Permission denied on Windows and fix it at the cause (a file still held open, or a POSIX-only step run on Windows); the test passes on Windows, macOS and Linux in CI; nothing is skipped or loosened

findings.body: The renamed lifecycle test does not arrange a sharing violation or verify that one occurred, so removing this retry can still leave it passing whenever polling misses the race. The existing tests in tests/test_codex_record_retry.py:25 exercise failures of os.replace in the writer, not this reader. Add a controlled regression that makes the record temporarily unreadable, releases it, and verifies that the real polling path reaches the existing cleanup assertions. It should fail with the pre-fix reader and pass with this change; otherwise the Windows failure this branch addresses remains unguarded under the requested test audit.
findings.title: Not done: Regression test for Windows record-read sharing violations

why: tests/test_macos_app_server.py::test_12_a_dead_driver_leaves_no_app_server_behind fails on Windows CI with PermissionError (Errno 13) on a temp file, so main is red on Windows
